title: Progressive Output Guarantees & Tool Invocation Shims — Acceptance Criteria
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Scope: Define deterministic acceptance criteria that validate progressive/partial streaming outputs and the behavior of function/tool invocation handshakes. This ticket captures the product-level requirements for how model-issued structured fragments are anchored to schemas, how tool/function calls are negotiated and retried, and the expected error and resume semantics. Non-goals: full SDK changes, infra capacity provisioning (handled in ENG tickets), and UI polish beyond debug surfaces.
background: Customers building agent-style flows reported two failure modes in recent incidents: (1) downstream tool handlers receiving truncated/incomplete JSON fragments during streaming which caused hard failures, and (2) duplicate tool invocations from retry logic when partial commit semantics were unclear. We need acceptance criteria so engineering can validate runtime changes that prevent these issues while preserving low-latency streaming behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Envelope anchoring: Every streamed fragment emitted by the model must include a monotonically increasing fragment_id and a total_sequence_hint when available. Tests must assert sequence monotonicity across network reconnects.

2) Checkpoint tokens: The runtime must emit checkpoint tokens at configurable intervals (default: every 512 tokens or when a fragment boundary occurs). Acceptance tests assert that resume-from-checkpoint results in re-emission starting at the next uncommitted fragment without duplicating previously committed tool calls.

3) Tool-call handshake: Tool/function invocations must follow a 3-phase handshake: (offer -> accept/decline -> commit). The runtime must never deliver an 'offer' more than once to the same tool instance without a prior explicit commit/abort acknowledgement. Acceptance test simulates flakey network and asserts single commit per logical invocation.

4) Partial-object repair: When a streaming fragment violates the declared schema mid-stream (malformed JSON or missing required fields), the runtime must either (a) emit a repair attempt (re-emit corrected fragment) and mark previous fragment as superseded, or (b) emit a structured error frame with error_code and human_readable_reason. Tests must cover both modes and ensure clients can deterministically choose repair vs fail behavior.

5) Idempotency keys: All tool invocations originating from the runtime must include an idempotency_key derived from the session_id + fragment_id + attempt_counter. Acceptance tests verify that retry of identical idempotency_key results in at-most-once tool execution semantics (simulated tool backend honors idempotency header).

6) Backpressure & graceful degradation: The runtime must expose backpressure signals to the model-serving layer. When downstream tool queues exceed thresholds, the system should either (a) pause streaming and emit a 'PAUSED' envelope, or (b) degrade to non-streaming buffered mode. Tests must validate both behaviors and measure <5% increase in token latency when degrading on synthetic workloads.

7) Observability hooks: Each fragment, checkpoint, handshake transition, and error frame must be emitted as a telemetry event with fields: fragment_id, session_id, model_variant, route, latency_ms, and outcome. Acceptance requires test dashboards to show per-route fragment success rate >=99.5 in staged environment.

8) Resume semantics: After client reconnect or transient runtime failover, resume-from-checkpoint must guarantee no lost fragments and provide clear dedupe behavior — acceptance tests assert identical consumer-visible object sequence when replayed from checkpoint vs original live stream.

9) Format negotiation: On session start, the runtime must negotiate output envelope schema version and supported framing modes with the client. Tests must include backward-compatibility cases (old client, new server) and forward-compatibility (new client, old server) and define fallback behavior.

10) Error classification & operator playbook: Errors must be classified as recoverable, repairable, or terminal. Acceptance requires an attached operator playbook stub and a simulated incident runbook validating that recoverable errors auto-retry, repairable errors trigger repair logic, and terminal errors escalate to alerts within 1 minute.

11) End-to-end e2e: Run end-to-end acceptance harness that exercises model generation -> streaming fragments -> tool handshake -> tool execution -> commit. Success criteria: no duplicate tool invocations in 10,000 simulated sessions and 99.9% successful commit rate under baseline load (50 RPS).
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope framing: verify fragment_id sequencing, checkpoint insertion, and sequence hints.
Integration: simulate flaky network between runtime and tool execution service and assert idempotency keys prevent duplicates.
Chaos: kill runtime worker mid-stream, assert resume-from-checkpoint recovers without missed commits.
Load: run 50 RPS e2e across three model variants to validate latency and success rate targets.
Compatibility matrix tests: combinations of envelope v1/v2, framed/unframed streaming, and SDK client versions.
Manual QA: design/PM review of error frames and operator playbook for clarity and actionable steps.
validation_metrics: fragment_success_rate: percentage of fragments that parse and pass schema validation (target >= 99.5%).
tool_commit_dup_rate: ratio of duplicate tool executions per 10k invocations (target <= 0.01%).
resume_reconciliation_time: time between reconnect and first validated fragment (target <= 300ms median).
stream_latency_impact: median token latency difference when backpressure/degrade mode triggered (target < 5% increase).
operator_alert_time: time from terminal error to page (target <= 60s).
decisions: Adopt lightweight envelope framing (fragment_id + fragment_type + sequence_hint) rather than fully nested chunked JSON to reduce client parsing complexity.
Use explicit idempotency_key for all tool invocations; do not rely solely on client-provided ids.
Default checkpoint cadence: 512 tokens or fragment boundary — configurable per-tenant via runtime config.
Repair-first strategy for schema violations in non-security-critical flows; emit structured error frames for security-sensitive failures.
Telemetry events will be emitted at sample rate 1.0 in staging and 0.1 in prod until rollout window completes.
Backpressure path: prefer pause-with-envelopes for interactive low-latency apps and buffered-nonstreaming mode for batch-oriented flows; allow route-level override.
Require security review for idempotency header formats because they include session-derived values (security_review_required=true).
